title: Harmonize chroma voice, introduce modular micro-elevation geometry, and condense typography for high-density components
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary:
This ticket consolidates our visual foundation for dense UI surfaces (tables, compact forms, button rows, and small cards). We will: 1) define a minimal "chroma voice" for primary/neutral/accent families with three anchored tones each, 2) introduce a modular micro-elevation geometry (4-step grid tuned for surface stacking at <8px gutters), and 3) condense the typographic scale for compact components (tighten line-height, reduce inter-step deltas). The goal is to reduce visual noise in dense layouts, make contrast predictable across palettes, and provide a safe backward-compatible migration path for existing components.
background:
Rationale and signals:
- Multiple product teams reported perceived contrast and weight inconsistencies in dense table rows and toolbar clusters after the last palette tweak.
- Percy visual regressions are concentrated in small-size buttons, sparklines, and data rows where token aliases diverge.
- Current elevation steps are uneven for compact layouts; shadows either read too strong or vanish at small scales.
- Accessibility audit highlighted borderline contrast for 12px labels on certain accents in high-density modes.

Previous attempts to 'tune' tokens per-component increased maintenance and caused fragmentation. This work aims for a compact, composable set of anchors to avoid per-component token proliferation.
decision_record:
Decisions made so far:
- Adopt 'chroma voice' pattern: each color family will expose three anchors (base, muted, emphasis) with semantics (background, border, emphasis).
- Micro-elevation grid: 0 (flat), 1 (ambient thin), 2 (soft lift), 3 (card lift). Shadows will use a single direction and scaled blur to avoid heavy contrast at small sizes.
- Typographic condensation: introduce 'compact' scale with -1 step for small components: reduce vertical rhythm by 8-12% and decrease letter-spacing by 0.5-1px for small caps.
- Compatibility: create alias tokens that map old token names to new anchors and include a runtime fallback in console themes to avoid immediate visual breaks.

Trade-offs considered:
- Narrower token set reduces flexibility but greatly simplifies QA and rollout.
- Stronger shadow normalization sacrifices some depth expressiveness for consistency in small components.
- Compact typography may require copy tweaks in a handful of legacy modals; decided acceptable for net UX improvement.
migration_plan:
Phased rollout:
Phase A - Design + Tests (this ticket): finalize token values, update Sketch/Figma libs, author migration docs and per-component deltas.
Phase B - Staging Canary: engineering implements aliases and theme flags (ENG-40212). Deploy to staging and run visual snapshots.
Phase C - Gradual Enablement: enable compact theme for 10% of internal org (console) and monitor regressions and support tickets.
Phase D - Full Release: flip default, publish migration guide, and remove aliases after 3 cycles.

Mapping & fallback strategy (examples):
- OLD: color-accent-600 -> NEW: chroma/accent/emphasis (alias: color-accent-600)
- OLD: surface-elevation-3 -> NEW: micro-elevation/3 (alias: surface-elevation-3)
- OLD: type-scale-12 -> NEW: type-compact/11 (alias: type-scale-12)
tokens_sample:
Proposed anchor tokens (human-readable):
- chroma/neutral/base = #11121A (used for high-emphasis text)
- chroma/neutral/muted = #5B606E (secondary text / border)
- chroma/neutral/bg = #F5F6F8 (card background for dense lists)
- chroma/accent/base = #0078D4
- chroma/accent/emphasis = #005FA3
- chroma/accent/muted = #7FB1E9

Micro-elevation (CSS token names):
- micro-elevation/0 = none
- micro-elevation/1 = 0 1px 2px rgba(16,20,24,0.04)
- micro-elevation/2 = 0 2px 6px rgba(16,20,24,0.06)
- micro-elevation/3 = 0 6px 18px rgba(16,20,24,0.10)

Typography (compact scale overrides):
- type-compact/12: 12px / 16px line-height / tracking -0.2px
- type-compact/14: 14px / 18px line-height / tracking -0.15px
acceptance_criteria:
- Design tokens published into figma tokens lib and approved by design lead.
- Percy snapshots: <1.5% failing diffs across core console screens after alias-backed rollout in staging.
- WCAG 2.1 AA contrast pass for all text sizes >= 12px in compact mode.
- Runtime alias layer implemented (ENG-40212) and feature-flagged for gradual rollout.
- Migration docs and component-by-component delta table published in Confluence.
- At least one consumer team (Billing) to complete migration feedback loop during canary.
open_questions:
- Should we expose an explicit 'compact' theme toggle in the console settings or rely on responsive breakpoints?
- Are micro-elevation tokens sufficient for third-party embedded widgets that rely on multiple directional shadows?
- Do we need to ship a deprecation schedule for legacy token sets and how long should aliases remain?
- Will condensed typography affect translations in RTL languages for small UI elements?
